items.title: Nemesis Boss Mechanic — persistent antagonist identity across runs
items.summary: Track per-boss kill counts locally; if a player dies to the same boss 3+ times without killing it, that boss becomes their "Nemesis" — flagged on the 3s cutscene card, with a 🎯 icon beside the boss health bar in-run. Killing your Nemesis awards 3× boss-kill coins and unlocks a new NEMESIS SLAIN achievement. Boss cutscene cards also gain a personal kill-count line: FIRST ENCOUNTER / VETERAN (5×) / EXECUTIONER (10×). This transforms bosses from repeating wave events into recurring antagonists the player has a personal relationship with, which is the deepest narrative memory layer available without a live-service backend.
items.recipe: Add `getBossKillRecord()` / `saveBossKillRecord()` to `src/storage.js` (localStorage `cod-boss-kills-v1`), define nemesis threshold (3 deaths, 0 kills) as a pure check, update `src/App.jsx` boss-wave start to read/write record + set `gs.nemesisBossType`, update boss cutscene card in `src/App.jsx` to show kill count line + NEMESIS badge, update `src/drawGame.js` boss health bar rendering to add 🎯 prefix when `gs.nemesisBossType === boss.type`, add NEMESIS_SLAIN achievement in `src/constants.js`, and award 3× coins on nemesis kill in the boss-kill block of the game loop.

items.title: Run Brain Experiment Follow-Through Loop — close the advice → action → result loop
items.summary: RunBrain currently produces a `nextExperiment` suggestion on every death screen but has no mechanism to check whether the player acted on it. On run start, save the last `nextExperiment` to localStorage (`cod-last-experiment-v1`). During the run, compare the player's actual config (starter weapon, first perk chosen, mode) against the suggestion. If it matches, add a "🧪 EXPERIMENT" chip to the HUD. At death, show "Experiment followed / diverged / matched" in RunCoach alongside the follow-through stat. This is the missing feedback arc that makes the AI feel like it learns rather than just talks — and it's entirely local, zero tokens, zero new backend.
items.recipe: Add `saveExperimentIntent(suggestion)` / `loadExperimentIntent()` to `src/storage.js` (key `cod-last-experiment-v1`), call save in DeathScreen on render, add `matchesExperiment(config, intent)` pure fn in `src/utils/runBrain.js`, call it in App.jsx on first perk chosen / first shop to set `gs._experimentMatched`, pass `experimentMatched` into `buildRunCoach()`, render 🧪 chip in `src/components/HUD.jsx` when `gs._experimentMatched !== undefined`, and surface result line on DeathScreen RunCoach card.

items.title: Aim Flow State Ring — visible precision mastery expression on the player character
items.summary: `gs.precisionStreak` exists and already awards coins, but the only feedback is a floating text message. A precision streak ≥ 5 deserves a visible ambient indicator: a subtle crosshair glow ring around the player sprite that intensifies with streak depth (streak 5 = faint, streak 10 = full glow, streak 15+ = pulsing). At streak 10+, enemies within aim range get a subtle highlight on their center hit zone showing the player where the precision window is. This is the most player-skill-affirming addition possible — it makes mastery visible without changing balance, and creates a distinct visual moment when flow state breaks.
items.recipe: In `src/drawGame.js`, after the player sprite is drawn, check `gs.precisionStreak >= 5` — if so, draw a `ctx.arc` stroke ring at player position with alpha proportional to `Math.min(1, streak/15)` and a color lerp from `#88FFFF` to `#FF88FF`. At streak >= 10, for each visible enemy within 200px, draw a small 6px ring at `(enemy.x, enemy.y - enemy.h/2 * 0.35)` with low alpha (0.25) using `#FFFFFF`. No game-state changes needed — reads existing `gs.precisionStreak`.

items.title: Mutation × Difficulty Compound Brief — contextual pre-run intelligence
items.summary: `getDifficultyBriefing()` in runBrain already produces per-difficulty run stats from history. The missing synthesis: cross-reference the current weekly mutation with difficulty history to produce a compound one-liner like "NIGHTMARE × Corrosive Rounds — your avg wave drops 40% at this combo (3 prior runs)." Players with no history get a generic mutation warning. This elevates the pre-run intel from raw stats to personalized risk assessment, directly answering "should I play on NIGHTMARE this week?" without any LLM spend.
items.recipe: Add `getMutationDifficultyBrief(mutation, difficulty, runHistory)` to `src/utils/runBrain.js`: filter runHistory for runs at that difficulty + mutation active week, compute avgWave delta vs non-mutation runs, return a one-sentence compound brief. Expose `getActiveMutation()` from `src/constants.js` (or use the existing `getWeeklyGauntlet()` mutation field). Render in HomeV2 difficulty picker below `getDifficultyBriefing()` as a small italic line when mutation is active.

items.title: Formation Flavor Text in Wave Preview Card — narrative wave identity
items.summary: Wave director spawns already get formation identity (flank/pincer/surge — S70), but the wave incoming preview card shows only count/event/boss hints. Mapping formation type → flavor descriptor makes each wave feel narratively distinct: "SURGE — overwhelming force," "PINCER — split attack," "FLANK — pressure from the sides." This is 8 lines of code for a meaningfully richer wave announcement that teaches players what to expect from each formation while they're already reading the card.
items.recipe: In `src/App.jsx`, when setting `gs._wavePreviewCard`, read `gs._lastFormationLabel` (add a 1-line ref update in `waveDirector.js`'s `resolveFormation` call), map it to a short descriptor object `{flank: 'pressure from the sides', pincer: 'split attack', surge: 'overwhelming force'}`, and append the descriptor as a new `formationHint` field on the preview card. Render it in `src/drawGame.js` wave preview card block as a small italic subtitle line.
